site.name: Alex Rivers
site.headline: Fast, reliable plugins for Paper & Spigot servers.
site.tagline: Server software that stays out of the way — no lag spikes, no bloated configs, no surprises at 3am.
site.about: I've been writing Java for Minecraft servers since 2019. I focus on Paper-first plugins: async where it matters, minimal dependencies, and APIs other developers can build on. When I'm not patching a scheduler, I'm profiling one.

projects.title: AetherQueue
projects.tagline: Async, priority-aware join queue for Paper networks.
projects.body:
## Overview
AetherQueue replaces the default login queue with an async, priority-aware queue built for networks running multiple Paper servers behind Velocity. Players see their position and estimated wait in the action bar while the queue drains.

## Key mechanics
- **Async by default** — queue state is handled off the main thread, so a burst of joins never blocks gameplay.
- **Priority passes** — permission-based tiers (`aetherqueue.priority.1`–`3`) with configurable weights.
- **Reservation window** — slots are held for 90 seconds, preventing ghost entries when a client disconnects mid-join.
- **Live position** — action bar updates once per second, throttled to four packets per player.

## Installation
1. Drop `AetherQueue.jar` into your proxy's `plugins/` folder.
2. Restart once to generate `config.yml`, then set your queue size and server names.
3. Run `/aq reload` after changes — no restart required.

Requires Java 21 and Paper 1.21+. Anonymous metrics are opt-out.

projects.title: NexusBridge
projects.tagline: Presence, shared chat and server switches across a Velocity network.
projects.body:
## Overview
NexusBridge keeps presence, shared chat and server-switch requests in sync across a Velocity network. It uses Redis pub/sub for messaging and a small in-memory fallback for single-server testing.

## Key mechanics
- **Zero-config discovery** — servers register themselves on startup and publish their current player counts.
- **Redis-backed presence** — one key per player, so a crashed server drops its entries automatically via TTL.
- **Safe transfers** — the destination must acknowledge a reservation before the proxy moves the player.
- **Developer API** — `NexusBridge.send(player, "survival")` for plugin authors, plus `/bridge send` for staff.

## Installation
1. Install the bridge jar on Velocity and the companion jar on every Paper server.
2. Set the same `redis.uri` and `network.id` in each `config.yml`.
3. Restart, then run `/bridge status` to confirm discovery.

Requires Paper 1.20.4+, Velocity 3.3+, Java 17+ and Redis 6+.

projects.title: PixelHolo
projects.tagline: Packet-based floating displays with zero entity overhead.
projects.body:
## Overview
PixelHolo renders floating text, item and block displays without armor stands or per-tick entity updates. Displays are packed into a single packet batch per player and only re-sent when they change.

## Key mechanics
- **Packet-first** — text is sent as display entities, not armor stands, so there is no collision or AI cost.
- **Per-player visibility** — show displays only to a permission group, world, or radius.
- **Animations** — bob, spin and typewriter effects are evaluated server-side at 10 Hz, not every tick.
- **In-game editor** — `/holo edit` opens a chat-driven editor with live preview.

## Installation
1. Drop `PixelHolo.jar` into `plugins/`.
2. Run `/holo create welcome` and follow the prompts.
3. Tune `update-interval` in `config.yml` if you run more than 200 displays.

Requires Paper 1.20.6+ and Java 21. PlaceholderAPI is optional.

projects.title: WardenEye
projects.tagline: Explainable movement and combat telemetry for staff review.
projects.body:
## Overview
WardenEye is a lightweight telemetry layer for detecting impossible movement, reach and autoclicker patterns. It does not ban anyone — it flags, explains and hands the evidence to your staff.

## Key mechanics
- **Explainable flags** — every alert includes the sample window and the maths behind it.
- **Low overhead** — checks run every other tick and sample only players in combat.
- **Staff review queue** — `/eye review` shows recent flags with replay-style coordinates.
- **Discord webhook** — batched alerts, grouped by player, with a configurable threshold.

## Installation
1. Drop `WardenEye.jar` into `plugins/`.
2. Set your webhook URL in `config.yml` (optional).
3. Run `/eye reload` and watch the first hour of flags before tuning thresholds.

Requires Paper 1.21+ and Java 21. WardenEye is not a replacement for a full anticheat.

projects.title: CraftBench
projects.tagline: A GUI recipe editor that saves without a restart.
projects.body:
## Overview
CraftBench is a recipe editor for server owners who are tired of hand-writing YAML. Build shaped and shapeless recipes in a chest GUI, preview the result, and save without restarting.

## Key mechanics
- **GUI editor** — drag ingredients into a 3×3 grid, set the output and save.
- **Namespace-aware** — recipes are stored under your own namespace so datapacks and other plugins never collide.
- **Live reload** — `/bench reload` rebuilds the recipe registry in place.
- **Import** — paste an existing recipe JSON and CraftBench converts it to an editable grid.

## Installation
1. Drop `CraftBench.jar` into `plugins/`.
2. Run `/bench` to open the editor.
3. Review `recipes/` before deploying to production.

Requires Paper 1.20.4+ and Java 17+. Does not modify vanilla recipes unless you ask it to.

projects.title: PaperBench
projects.tagline: JMH benchmarks for Paper plugins, without booting a server.
projects.body:
## Overview
PaperBench is a JMH harness for benchmarking Paper plugin code without booting a full server. It ships with fixtures for the event bus, scheduler and item meta operations, plus a tiny report viewer.

## Key mechanics
- **Realistic fixtures** — mocked Paper registries and a deterministic tick loop.
- **Warmup-aware** — JMH handles warmup, forks and percentile reporting.
- **Regression gate** — fail CI when a benchmark regresses by more than a configurable percentage.
- **Report viewer** — `paperbench report` turns JMH JSON into a single static HTML file.

## Installation
```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/paperbench
cd paperbench
./gradlew jmh
```

Add `paperbench` as a `testImplementation` dependency to benchmark your own plugin.

Requires JDK 21 and Gradle 8+. Built for Paper 1.21, works with Spigot APIs.
